subject: Recap: Performance SLOs (p95/p99) — hosted API vs current provider
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <jordan@finlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Recap from today's call — p95/p99 targets and test scope

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the call today — really helpful to see Redwood's runtime and the routing options. As promised, here’s a quick recap of our perf requirements and where we currently sit:

- Business goal: real-time assistant across our analytics product (web UI + streaming mobile).
- Targets: p95 end-to-end <= 300ms, p99 end-to-end <= 700ms.
- Current provider (internal metrics): p95 ~450ms, p99 ~900ms (includes network + inference + postprocessing).
- Throughput: steady-state 30 RPS, peak 120 RPS for ~10-15min bursts during reports.
- Concurrent requests: typical concurrency 40, burst concurrency up to 200 across regions.
- Streaming: needed for progressive tokens on UI; we need partial token latencies to feel snappy (first-token < 150ms ideally).
- Auth/data: JWT-based auth, payloads average 600 tokens (max 2k tokens) with lightweight postprocessing in our service.

Next steps we agreed on:
1) Redwood runs a benchmark of hosted API against a set of sample payloads (I attached sample_payloads.json).
2) Compare Redwood hosted p95/p99 to our current provider baseline (I attached current_provider_metrics.csv).
3) Confirm whether streaming mode maintains p95 targets and what concurrency shaping you'd recommend.
4) Draft a mutual action plan — attaching a starter MAP (mutual_action_plan.xlsx).

We can make test data available in a staging workspace and grant a short-lived API key. Do you need anything else from our side to set up the run?

Thanks,
Jordan
Director of Engineering
Finlytics

---
Attachment: sample_payloads.json (3 payloads, avg token counts)
Attachment: current_provider_metrics.csv (recent week of p95/p99 samples)
Attachment: mutual_action_plan.xlsx (starter MAP)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan@finlytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap from today's call — p95/p99 targets and test scope

Thanks Jordan — this is perfect. Appreciate the concrete numbers and the attachments.

A few clarifying questions before we kick off the hosted benchmark:
- When you say p95/p99 end-to-end, is that measured from client-to-client through your gateway (i.e., includes your ingress network + postprocessing)? I want to make sure our comparison apples-to-apples.
- For streaming: do you measure the first-byte latency separately today? If not, can we start with first-token and steady-stream intervals?
- For burst concurrency, is the 200 concurrent requests mostly from a single region or across our multi-region footprint?

Proposed Redwood test plan (we can iterate):
1) Run three 1-hour soak tests on hosted API with your sample payloads: steady 30 RPS, medium burst 120 RPS, high concurrency 200 across two regions.
2) Collect client-side end-to-end p50/p95/p99 plus first-token times for streaming requests.
3) We'll also run a provider-side emulation (best-effort) to normalize network overhead differences; please share your preferred test region and a pcap/egress latency sample if possible.
4) Deliver a short report with recommended batching/quantization profile and a candidate config that meets p95 <= 300ms.

Aditya — looping you in on the test details and to own the hosted perf run and the streaming experiment. Would you be able to pick this up tomorrow?

Jordan — if that plan looks good I can stand up the hosted run and send a short test endpoint + temporary key. Also happy to sync a 30-min call to walk through the MAP.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com
+1 415-555-0134

---
Attachment: mutual_action_plan.xlsx

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: 
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap from today's call — p95/p99 targets and test scope

Thanks for the context — I can take the run. A couple of notes from an engineering perspective:

- We should make sure the test includes TLS + JWT auth hops to capture handshake costs for first-byte latency.
- For streaming, Redwood's hosted API exposes both a chunked HTTP stream and a WS option; we'll test chunked first (matches most browser flows).
- To emulate your current provider network overhead, please share one sample trace or a small latency matrix (client->provider egress) so we can add a sane synthetic delay when comparing.

Proposed timeline: I can provision the ephemeral test endpoints and a temporary key by tomorrow (Fri EOD), run the three soak tests on Monday, and provide results Tuesday. If that works for you, Jordan send the staging region and the trace.

I'll capture metrics: client-side request timestamps, server ingress, token emit times, model latency, and postprocessing times. I'll attach a short script to reproduce locally.

- Aditya
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: hosted_perf_run_instructions.md

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan@finlytics.com>

Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap from today's call — p95/p99 targets and test scope (confirmed)

Jordan — thanks for the quick replies earlier in the week and for sharing the files. Confirming next steps and immediate asks:

Action items (confirmed):
- Finlytics: share a small pcap or latency matrix (client egress to your staging) and confirm preferred test regions (us-west1 + us-east4). Also confirm whether the bursts are single-region or cross-region — you flagged likely cross-region, so we'll plan cross-region bursts.
- Redwood (Aditya): provision ephemeral hosted endpoints + temp key; run three 1-hour soak tests (steady 30 RPS, medium burst 120 RPS, high cross-region concurrency 200) and capture client-side end-to-end p50/p95/p99 and first-token times.
- Redwood (Marissa): update MAP with proposed timeline and next meeting slot (30m) to review results.

Benchmark expectations we will report against:
- Goal: p95 <= 300ms end-to-end on hosted API for steady and medium burst tests.
- For high cross-region concurrency we expect some tail degradation; we'll surface tradeoffs and recommended routing/burst policies.
- Streaming: first-token target <= 150ms; steady streaming throughput goals documented in the MAP.

I'll also capture a side-by-side baseline comparison against your current provider using the same payloads and synthetic network adjustments so we provide an apples-to-apples view.

Can you confirm the test region and send that latency matrix today so Aditya can start provisioning? If you prefer a quick 15-min call to unblock this, I'm free at 1:00pm PT today.

Thanks — looking forward to the run.

Marissa
